key_insight: An unfitted HHO method can accurately simulate elastic wave propagation across an imperfect, slipping interface without requiring the mesh to align with the interface.
engineering_relevance: This enables robust and high-order solid mechanics simulations on complex geometries while remaining stable across extreme interface compliancy contrasts and cut-cell configurations.
method: Duplicate unknowns in cut cells and use cell agglomeration to avoid tiny-cut instabilities.
Reconstruct local symmetric strain with a regularized interface stiffness matrix to enforce traction continuity and displacement slip.
Add interface stabilization and couple the semi-discrete scheme with Newmark or high-order SDIRK time integrators.
evidence_signal: The paper reports theoretical coercivity, continuity, and optimal h^{k+1} energy and h^{k+2} L2 convergence, confirmed numerically in 2D for k=1,2,3 and robustness over sixteen orders of magnitude in compliancy.
watch_item: The method is more complex to implement because it combines cut-cell agglomeration, doubled unknowns, and interface-specific stabilization, which may increase setup and assembly effort.
paper_title: An Unfitted Hybrid High-Order Method for the Elastodynamics Problem with Imperfect Interface
